absent.note: The C1002 X7R series datasheet (all 28 pages read) tabulates no DC-bias capacitance change; its overview only says X7R capacitance changes predictably with voltage. KEMET's per-part specification sheet plots a Capacitance Change vs. DC Voltage Bias curve (page 2), but it is a K-SIM simulation that page 4 says shows the typical response and is not a specification. No figure is recorded.

The C1002 X7R series datasheet has no absolute-maximum table. The 250 % dielectric withstanding voltage on page 16 is a 5 s production test, not a rating, and the storage and handling guidance on page 19 is not a storage-temperature limit. The per-part specification sheet has no absolute-maximum table either; its Dielectric Withstanding Voltage of 125 VDC is that 250 % test level.

notes:
Benchmark (a) uses this part as the 555's VCC bypass (/c_byp, parts.yaml CBYP).

The sources are KEMET's X7R commercial-grade series datasheet and KEMET's per-part specification sheet, which search.kemet.com generates on request; the per-part sheet settles what the series sheet leaves to it, the capacitance test voltage (1.0 Vrms) and aging referee time (48 hours), and states the TCC test's 0 VDC bias. Lifecycle is unknown: KEMET product pages now redirect to yageogroup.com, outside the kemet host allowlist (L21), and neither datasheet states a status. No DC-bias capacitance change is tabulated (the per-part sheet's DC-bias curve is a simulation KEMET says is not a specification), and KEMET publishes no absolute-maximum table: the rated voltage is ratings.recommended.voltage_rating.
